title: Scalar Carnot flow-lift factor is inverted: a hotter flow raises COP, and the batch twin disagrees
claim: ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor returns carnot_ref/carnot_flow (>1 above the 35 C reference, 1.586 at a 60 C flow and 0 C outdoor) while _batch_cop multiplies by carnot_flow/carnot_ref (<1), so every scalar COP priced at a flow above the reference (valved buffer, every DHW charge, a direct plant's curve) is boosted instead of derated and simulate_trajectory_batch disagrees with simulate_trajectory on 14 897 trajectory elements over the valved/combi/wood/coil arms. On the 50 published golden plans flow_lift_factor returned >1 on 1268 calls.
mechanism: thermal_model.py:3391 `return max(0.25, carnot_ref / carnot_flow)` against thermal_model.py:4483 `np.maximum(0.25, carnot_flow / carnot_ref)`. compute_cop (valve: flow_temp = tank), compute_cop_dhw (flow = tank water) and the curve-flow lift all route through flow_lift_factor; the batch twin, used for the solver's finite-difference gradient, carries the physical ratio. Consequences: the scalar objective prices hot storage cheaper the hotter it is (DHW COP 2.89 at 35 C, 4.26 at 55 C, 4.58 at 60 C at 0 C outdoor), and the gradient the solver follows is of a different physics than the objective it scores.
